newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks end higher on back of blue chips.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks end higher on back of blue chips.

text.p: Tokyo stocks ended Tuesday trade with healthy gains as buying of blue chips picked up, stamping out early morning losses, brokers said.
But they said trade was subdued as Tuesday was the last trading day for February delivery.
The Nikkei 225 rose 173.08 points or 0.92 percent to end at 19,070.07. Its March futures added 260 points to end at 19,120.
"Blue chips which had fallen too far in recent days were bought back and bank shares, which rose sharply late last week, gradually lost steam," said Merrill Lynch strategist Keiko Kondo.

The Nikkei benchmark slid in the morning, depressed by weak Nikkei 225 futures in Chicago as well as strength in the yen, which made the market brace for more profit-taking in recently battered high-technology shares.
The index fell as low as 18,775.90 before rebounding.

"Traders placed buy orders for Sony Corp, which led the most recent blue-chip rally, in order to test the market and the market responded in a positive way," said Yasuo Ueki, Nikko Securities general manager. "Buying spread to other global issues."
Sony added 200 yen to close at 8,780.

Brokers said despite renewed interest in global issues, a wait-and-see mood subdued activity. The market was waiting for testimony by U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan to the Senate Banking Committee on Wednesday, they said.
Greenspan is expected to describe the U.S. economy in upbeat terms but he could also utter words of caution about inflation and possibly the U.S. stock market.
Turnover fell to 424 million shares from Monday's 460 million as a result, brokers said.
Winners edged ahead of losers by 555 issues to 537, while 164 issues were unchanged.

Buying of bank sector 0#BNK.T stocks and other problem-loan laden sectors petered out after the shares were bolstered in recent sessions by news that the government is considering using public funds to boost the property market.
"Comments from the political sphere lifted the sectors, but in order to keep them climbing, concrete plans need to be announced," a "Big Four" broker said.
However, some brokers added that sharp declines seen in the past were unlikely to be repeated, unless the government decides to scrap the proposed measures to help solve the bad loan problem.

The ruling Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) and its allies reached an agreement on Tuesday to lift a decades-long ban on holding companies. An LDP official said that a bill to amend the anti-monopoly law would likely take effect within a year.

Guidelines to define what types of holding companies would still be prohibited have yet to be worked out. Changes in laws to enable financial institutions to set up holding firms once the amended anti-monopoly law takes effect have yet to be made.
"Until specific details are drawn up and firms start reshuffling, it will be difficult to assess the impact of the lifting of the ban on the market," Merrill's Kondo said.
Both Yoshitomi Pharmaceutical Industries Ltd and scandal-tainted drug company Green Cross Corp fell following news that they are planning to merge.
Yoshitomi fell 68 yen to 822 and Green Cross, the second largest percentage loser on the first section of the Tokyo bourse on Tuesday, fell 46 yen to 530.

Exchange officials said they were checking the share prices of the two drug firms as a standard procedure after an announcement of any important news which could affect stock prices. They said this was not specifically an investigation of possible insider trading.

Tokyo Disneyland operator Oriental Land Co Ltd closed 310 yen higher at 8,100, boosted by reports that it would decide at a board meeting on Tuesday to provide shareholders with tickets to its facilities. After the market closed, the firm announced it would distribute tickets to shareholders.

Semiconductor testing device maker Advantest Corp rose 120 yen to 6,520 while Nikon Corp, which makes semiconductor-related equipment as well as cameras, added 80 yen to close at 1,800. Both were helped by the comeback by Sony.
In sectors, precision instruments, fisheries, electric power, pulp/paper and insurance were the main gainers.
The retreaters were headed by air transport, securities, credit/lease, iron/steel and construction.

The broader TOPIX index added 2.07 points or 0.15 percent to end at 1,425.37. The Nikkei 300 firmed 0.46 point, or 0.17 percent to close at 273.55. The second section index rose 3.70 points or 0.21 percent to finish at 1,741.36 on a turnover of 8.77 million shares. There were 8.56 million shares traded on Monday.
The over-the-counter index stood at 1,211.75, up 4.29 points or 0.36 percent in late Tokyo.
-- Masako Iijima, Tokyo Equities Desk +81-3-3432-9052
